message.reasoning:
We need P(defective | X+, Y-). Use Bayes.

Let D = defective, N = not defective.

P(D)=1/3, P(N)=2/3.

Given D: P(X+)=3/4, P(Y+)=2/3, Y- =1-2/3=1/3. Assuming independence conditional on D: P(X+,Y-) = (3/4)*(1/3)=3/12=1/4.

Given N: P(X+)=1/4, P(Y+)=1/3, Y- =2/3. So P(X+,Y-) = (1/4)*(2/3)=2/12=1/6.

Now compute posterior: P(D | X+,Y-) = P(D)*P(X+,Y- | D) / [P(D)*P(X+,Y- | D) + P(N)*P(X+,Y- | N)]

= (1/3)*(1/4) / [(1/3)*(1/4) + (2/3)*(1/6)].

Compute numerator: 1/12.

Denominator: 1/12 + (2/3)*(1/6) = 1/12 + (2/18)=1/12 + 1/9.

Find common denominator 36: 1/12 =3/36. 1/9=4/36. Sum =7/36.

So posterior = (3/36)/(7/36) =3/7.

Thus answer A.
